title: Towards Integrating Soft X-ray Tomography with Infrared Imaging for Building Whole Cell Models
content: Soft X-ray tomography (SXT) is an emerging imaging technique with the potential to transform cell modeling by providing high-resolution, three-dimensional reconstructions of cellular ultrastructure. With spatial resolution around 50 nm, SXT offers detailed visualization of cellular organelles without the need for contrast agents or fixation [1-3]. The recent development of the SXT-100 microscope, a compact device suitable for routine use in laboratory settings, by SiriusXT, has greatly expanded access to this powerful tool in labs, enabling studies in diseases, drug effects, and cellular differentiation [4]. Easier access has enabled its integration with other imaging techniques, such as cryo-fluorescence and electron microscopy, for more accurate, multi-scale models of cellular processes [5]. Along these lines, our efforts are directed towards the potential integration of infrared (IR) spectroscopic imaging data with SXT imaging results for generating whole cell tomograms with enhanced chemical specificity.
